chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Mis'a ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If a slave performed Hajj ten times, the obligation of Hajj of Islam would still remain upon him if he had the means to do so.
And if a boy (who was not yet of age) performed Hajj for ten years, then reached puberty, the obligation of Hajj of Islam would be upon him.
And if a slave performed Hajj ten times, then was freed, the obligation of Hajj of Islam would be upon him if he had the means to do so.
ai.seo_question: Does Hajj performed by a slave or child count as the obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies that Hajj performed by slaves or pre-pubescent boys, while virtuous, does not discharge the primary obligatory duty (Fard al-Ain); the obligation remains pending until they gain full legal capacity. It establishes a clear jurisprudential distinction between voluntary acts of worship and the definitive religious duty, which only becomes binding upon emancipation for slaves or puberty for boys, provided they possess the means. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of obligation despite prior worship, ensuring the completeness of one's religious portfolio.
